title: diagnostic heatmap and correlator panel wireframes & grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposal and rough wireframes for a Diagnostic Heatmap + Correlator panel inside the Console debugging surface. Goal: give engineers a fast way to see where errors (timeouts, 5xx, model errors, hallucinations) cluster and what request metadata correlates most strongly with those clusters, with one click path to payload inspection and traces.

Why this is different / gaps addressed:
- Existing views show sample traces or single-request playback. Hard to answer: are errors driven by specific routes, prompt lengths, model variants, regions, or client SDKs?
- Teams waste time opening many traces to find patterns. Heatmap + correlator aims to compress multi-dimensional signals into a visual correlation-first triage flow.

High-level UX flow (user story):
- As an SRE/ML engineer, I land on the Errors page for my org and want to quickly answer: are errors random or concentrated? If concentrated, what features (model, route, region, prompt size) co-occur?
- I use time + cohort filters, inspect heatmap hotspots, open correlator panel to see ranked features, then open sample payloads or jump to distributed traces / cached KV snapshots.

Wireframe notes (layout):
- Top bar: global filters (time range, environment: hosted/dedicated/private, model family, route prefix, status codes toggle: timeout|5xx|model-error|policy-block).
- Left column (vertical): dimension filters + quick-slices (by route, model, client-region, SDK-version, prompt-length buckets, quantization-profile).
- Main pane: multi-axis heatmap grid. Two alternate modes: 
  1) Time x Route heatmap (rows = top N routes, columns = time buckets) intensity = error rate or error count normalized by requests.
  2) Dimension correlation matrix (rows = features, columns = top error types) showing Pearson-like correlation score colored by sign/magnitude.
- Right panel (collapsable): Correlator details: ranked list of features (e.g., model=redwood-xl-v1, prompt_len>2048, cache_miss, region=eu-west-1) with a score, sample size, effect size (delta in error rate), and quick actions: "show sample requests", "open trace", "exclude from cohort".
- Bottom strip: timeline with annotation marks for deploys, config changes (rollouts), and capacity events. Hovering over a heatmap cell highlights matching traces in the timeline/trace viewer.

Interactions and microcopy:
- Hover cell -> tooltip: counts (errs/total), error rate %, top 3 sample routes/variants, top correlated features. CTA: "Explore cohort" (opens correlator and payload list).
- Correlator feature row: small sparkline of trend, confidence interval, link to query used to build this row. Action menu includes: "create alert", "open in query builder", "pin to dashboard".
- Payload inspector opens in modal showing request metadata, truncated prompt, token-level timings, model logs (if available), and the stack trace for 5xx. Buttons: "copy full request", "replay (sandbox)".

Backend / telemetry needs (high level):
- Aggregation pipeline that can compute per-route, per-model, per-region error counts in time buckets (1m/5m/1h).
- Feature extraction for correlator: categorical (route, model, region, sdk_version, quant_profile), numeric buckets (prompt_length, top_k, temperature), binary flags (cache_hit, fallback_used).
- Statistical test: compute lift = P(error | feature) - P(error) and percentile-based significance and minimum sample size filter. Store precomputed correlator results for interactive UI.

Example query (pseudo-SQL) for heatmap cell counts:
SELECT route, time_bucket('5m', ts) AS tb, count(*) AS requests, sum(is_error) AS errors
FROM requests
WHERE org_id = ? AND ts BETWEEN ? AND ?
GROUP BY route, tb
ORDER BY route, tb

Correlator score (pseudo):
score = (errors_with_feature / requests_with_feature) - (global_errors / global_requests) 
apply bootstrapped CI and require requests_with_feature >= 50

Sample data fields to surface in UI (minimum):
- request_id, ts, org_id, route, model, model_variant, response_status (timeout|5xx|model_error|ok), latency_ms, prompt_length, token_count, cache_hit (bool), fallback_used (bool), client_region, sdk_version, quant_profile, server_host

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- User can toggle heatmap mode (time x route) and see correct error intensity for selected time range.
- Correlator panel shows top 10 features ranked by lift with sample sizes and effect size.
- Clicking a feature filters the heatmap/cohort and shows matching payloads (min 10 samples).
- From payload list user can open payload inspector and jump to traces if trace id exists.
- Alerts: from a correlator row, user can create a "cohort alert" that fires when lift > configurable threshold for X mins.

Backlog (prioritized) — grooming notes with rough estimates:
- UX: lo-fi wireframes and copy polish (Aisha) — 1d
- API: endpoint to return heatmap aggregates (route x time) + pagination (Infra) — 3d
- API: correlator job & storage (compute offline daily + on-demand) (Applied ML) — 5d
- UI: heatmap grid implementation + hover tooltips (Frontend) — 5d
- UI: correlator panel, ranking UI, quick actions (Frontend) — 3d
- Integration: payload inspector modal and trace link surface (Frontend + SRE) — 3d
- Alerts: create cohort alert flow + backend rule engine hook (Product + Infra) — 4d
- Tests + e2e: sample datasets and regression suite (QA) — 2d
Notes: estimates are team-days, dependent on availability of precomputed aggregates.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should the correlator compute pairwise interactions (e.g., model X prompt_len>2048) or only single-feature lift? Pairwise greatly increases compute/space.
- Minimum threshold for feature sample size — default 50 or 100?
- Alert ergonomics: should alerts be percentage lift or absolute error rate?
- How to surface privacy/PII risk in sample payloads (masking rules)?

Edge cases and hazards:
- Sparse routes: many routes with tiny traffic can dominate heatmap; show top-N by volume and provide "show all" toggle.
- Burst errors: short spikes may show high lift but low A/B confidence — expose CI / sample size prominently.
- Model fallback chains: if fallback_used true, correlate at both primary and fallback variants to avoid misleading attribution.

Mockup appendix (sketch text):
[Top] Global filters: | last 24h | env: hosted | model family: all | status: timeout,5xx |
[Left] Filters: routes (multiselect), model (multiselect), region, sdk version, prompt length slider
[Center] Heatmap: Rows = top 30 routes (sortable by error rate), Cols = 5m buckets. Color = error rate gradient (white->red). Hover cell: small popover with counts + top correlated features.
[Right] Correlator (expanded):
  1) model=redwood-xl-v1 — score +0.18 — 240 samples — delta err 12% -> action: show samples / create alert
  2) prompt_len>2048 — score +0.12 — 110 samples — delta err 8%
  3) cache_miss=true — score +0.07 — 520 samples

Follow-ups (next week):
- Sync with Applied ML to agree correlator score semantics (Marco)
- Wireframe polish and hi-fi mocks for final UX review (Lena)
- Inventory telemetry gaps (Samir) and create infra tickets for aggregation tables

Notes-to-self: keep the initial MVP narrow — time x route heatmap + single-feature correlator. If successful iterate to pairwise and clustering (error signatures) later.

References / similar ideas:
- Notebook used in RD-4321 where Marco prototyped bootstrap lift scoring.
- Console incident snapshot flows for deep-dive (see CONFLUENCE-Console/ERROR-UX-Notes).

End of doc.
